memory_candidates.content: PyMuPDF hermetic PDF fixtures cannot carry non-Latin-1 characters (math symbols like the U+2200/U+2203 binders) via page.insert_text(): with a base-14 font such as 'helv' the character is silently substituted with a middle dot (U+00B7), and with the built-in CJK font 'china-ss' it is dropped entirely. Neither failure raises. fitz.Font(name).has_glyph() is NOT a reliable predictor -- it reports a nonzero glyph id for U+2200 under 'helv' even though insert_text mangles it. The working hermetic path (no extra dependency, no system font file, no pymupdf_fonts package) is the TextWriter API: tw = fitz.TextWriter(page.rect); tw.append(pos, text, font=fitz.Font('helv'), fontsize=n); tw.write_text(page). Verified round-trip: the extracted text preserves the binder characters exactly. General lesson: for any PDF fixture asserting on extracted text, verify the round-trip through get_text() rather than trusting the source string literal -- a silently substituted glyph turns a two-condition test into a one-condition test with no visible failure.
